sentences.text:
This is the first bail application filed by applicant under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.03/2024, registered at Police Station- Mahila Thana,
District-Tikamgarh (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 376(2)(n) of the IPC.
2. Learned counsel appearing for applicant submitted that applicant and prosecutrix were in love relationship.
Later on, family members of prosecutrix learnt about their affair and they had assaulted the applicant.
It is submitted that though charge sheet has not been filed but investigation in respect of applicant is complete and he is in jail since 12.01.2024.
In these circumstances, applicant may be released on bail.
3. Learned Government Advocate appearing for the State opposed the bail application and has submitted that prosecutrix has repeatedly been raped by the applicant.

He read over the statement Ajay Ahirwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10565035/

4. Heard the counsel for the parties.
5.
Considering aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and also statement of prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C., bail application filed by the applicant, is allowed.

It is directed that applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his regular appearance before Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of trial.
